_what_the_26_were: 18 lazy chart wrappers whose row named the test of the canonical function three names down; 6 score_batch methods graded PROVEN in wave 1 on a file that never calls them; 1 drift explanation resting on a transitive justification; and BaseFeatureTransformer.fit, which is NOT a finding: its row honestly says 'none needed for the body' because the body is an abstract `pass`, and the verifier was misreading the test files mentioned in that explanation as its evidence. That false positive was fixed in the verifier rather than in the row.
_what_this_is: Grading wave 5. Not new units: these are rows that ALREADY carried a grade and a published CHECKED badge, and whose named test does not execute them. Found by scripts/verify_grade_attribution.py, which runs each named test file under coverage and asks whether the unit's body lines were reached.
_why_this_matters: A row's test_file is the evidence behind its badge. A row naming a test that never touches the unit is a claim with nothing behind it, which is the defect this library is audited for, one level up and in the surface built to prevent it. Across 415 graded rows the check confirmed 348 by line coverage, reported 40 as blind (38 class bodies, which execute at import before coverage starts, and 2 bodies excluded by configuration) and found 26.

vfairness.llm.scorers.ContextualStereoty.judgement: Executed for the first time by any test. The single-text score() path was thoroughly pinned and the batch path beside it was not pinned at all, although every aggregate comparison in the LLM fairness surface goes through the batch path: a divergence of one element there is a group disparity computed from values no caller could reproduce one at a time. Measured: all six agree with score() element by element across a corpus spanning both poles, a refusal, marker-free text, non-ASCII text and blank text. The two families answer a blank generation differently ON PURPOSE and both halves are pinned: a midpoint scale refuses it, because the centre of the scale is a measured value, and a presence detector reports a measured 0.0, because absence of the marker it looks for is evidence of absence.
vfairness.llm.scorers.ContextualStereoty.sabotage: Each of the six score_batch implementations replaced by np.zeros(len(texts)) in turn, a divergence with the right shape and dtype: 6 of 6 red. The first pass was 5 of 6, because every text in the corpus scored 0.0 for ContextualStereotypeScorer so a constant-zero batch matched its honest output; a scoring text was added and it then went red too. Restored: 25 passed.
vfairness.llm.scorers.ContextualStereoty.was: PROVEN with no sabotage, on tests/test_surface_grade_g000.py, which never calls score_batch (wave 1)

vfairness.llm.scorers.FramingScorer.scor.defect: Returned 0.5, the exact midpoint of the [0, 1] framing scale, for empty and whitespace-only text, while a REAL text carrying no framing marker two branches below correctly returned NaN. So 'the doctor was competent and kind' was refused and '' was scored. The carve-out justified itself 'on the same ground as KeywordSentimentScorer's empty-text carve-out', and that carve-out had been WITHDRAWN on 2026-09-17 by the argument that a midpoint is a measured value and not an absence. The cross-reference outlived the thing it pointed at. The mechanism is the one this method was written to fix: two groups of empty generations reported 0.5 against 0.5, delta 0.0, assessed=True.
vfairness.llm.scorers.FramingScorer.scor.fix: The blank branch returns None, so score() answers NaN, which is what the marker-free branch already did. The docstring paragraph that cited the withdrawn precedent is replaced by one recording that it was withdrawn.
vfairness.llm.scorers.FramingScorer.scor.sabotage: The 0.5 return restored: 3 red (the midpoint-family pin for FramingScorer, the blank/marker-free consistency pin, and the refusal-announcement pin). Restored: 25 passed.

vfairness.operations.monitoring.drift.Fa.judgement: Executed directly for the first time. The row it supersedes carried no test of its own and justified itself transitively: 'none: the explainer's own three-state behaviour is already pinned by tests/test_readiness2_explainer.py and tests/test_explain_partial_runs.py'. Those files pin the EXPLAINER and neither reaches this method. Measured here: on a constant series where no scale could be analysed, drift_detected is None and the summary reads 'Drift COULD NOT CHECK: no drift test ran, so there is no verdict', and on a genuine mean shift it reports detected with a score. Honest, and now pinned.
vfairness.operations.monitoring.drift.Fa.sabotage: The could-not-check summary rewritten to 'Drift NOT DETECTED: the data looks stable': 1 red. The FIRST version of the pin stayed GREEN under this same sabotage, because it searched str(report) for 'COULD NOT CHECK' and that phrase occurs three times in the rendered report; it now asserts on report.summary, the line a reader sees first. Restored: 13 passed.
vfairness.operations.monitoring.drift.Fa.was: SEMI-PROVEN on a transitive justification, with no test of its own (wave 2)
